nodes.label: SwiftLint Configuration (opt-in rule set, strict)
nodes.rationale: Uses only_rules with a curated opt-in list (no default rule set), strict: true so warnings fail the lint, indented switch cases, and excludes .build and xcode directories.

nodes.label: Docs TOC Scroll-spy Script
nodes.rationale: Asciidoctor docinfo footer injected into generated doc pages; highlights the active TOC link (toc-active class) on scroll using requestAnimationFrame throttling.

nodes.label: aerospace CLI EBNF Grammar (complgen)
nodes.rationale: Hand-maintained (despite the name, not generated) EBNF-like grammar of all aerospace CLI subcommands, managed by complgen and consumed by build-shell-completion.sh; must be edited by hand when adding a command since the ANTLR grammar was replaced by a hand-written lexer/parser.

nodes.label: AeroSpace App Target (XcodeGen project.yml)
nodes.rationale: macOS application target (deployment 13.0) depending on the AppBundle SPM product; INFOPLIST_KEY_LSUIElement=YES so it runs as an agent app with no Dock icon; com.apple.security.app-sandbox=false because the Accessibility API does not work in sandboxed apps; CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY and MARKETING_VERSION are injected via XCODEGEN_* env vars; Release config treats warnings as errors.

nodes.label: Client/Server Split (aerospace CLI vs AeroSpace.app)
nodes.rationale: Args are parsed on the client for --help and early exit, sent over a Unix socket, then re-parsed on the server via the same code in Sources/Common/cmdArgs; the shared-parser constraint is why arg parsing lives in Common/ so both client and server link it.

nodes.label: Command Pipeline (three-place command definition)
nodes.rationale: A command is defined in three places (Common cmdArgs struct, AppBundle Command impl, docs adoc); adding or renaming a command without touching all three breaks the build or the test.sh uncommitted-generated-files check.

nodes.label: Focus Subsystem (LiveFocus/FrozenFocus)
nodes.rationale: Focus changes pair setFocus(to:) (tree model update) with Window.nativeFocus() (AX raise + app activate); commands respect --window-id/--workspace env before falling back to the global focus.

nodes.label: Refresh Sessions (focus + layout reconciliation)
nodes.rationale: runLightSession is single-flight: it cancels any in-flight heavy refresh, runs the command body, relayouts, syncs focus, then reschedules a heavy session; tree-mutating code paths must route through it so on-focus-changed/broadcast machinery stays consistent.

nodes.label: Swift Strict Concurrency Convention
nodes.rationale: Package.swift enables NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault and strictMemorySafety; most mutable globals are @MainActor and the few nonisolated(unsafe) globals require the unsafe keyword.

nodes.label: Test and Lint Pipeline (test.sh/lint.sh/generate.sh)
nodes.rationale: test.sh is CI-equivalent (warnings-as-errors build, tests, CLI smoke tests, lint, generate, and an uncommitted-generated-files check); lint.sh runs swiftformat, a Task.init ban, swiftlint in check mode (no auto-fix), and periphery (currently skipped on macOS 14/15/26).

nodes.label: Tree Model Subsystem (TreeNode/Workspace/Window)
nodes.rationale: Every node records lastAppliedLayoutPhysicalRect and lastAppliedLayoutVirtualRect so many commands can read cached geometry without re-querying AX.

nodes.label: SPM Library + Xcode Launcher Infrastructure
nodes.rationale: SPM only builds libraries and CLI apps, not App Bundles, and Swift LSP only supports SPM projects — so all code is pushed into the SPM library and the Xcode project is a tiny launcher skeleton generated from project.yml.

nodes.label: Entry Point Build Scripts
nodes.rationale: Debug builds use SPM only (build-debug.sh); release builds use Xcode (build-release.sh); build-docs.sh, build-shell-completion.sh and generate.sh produce the site/man pages, completions, and generated project files respectively.

nodes.label: Self-signed Codesign Certificate (aerospace-codesign-certificate)
nodes.rationale: Needed only for App Bundle builds; debug builds run from the terminal unsigned. Created in Keychain Access as a Self-Signed Root, Code Signing certificate.

nodes.label: Docs Site Deployment (GitHub Pages)
nodes.rationale: Deploys only on tagged releases (v*-Beta.adrianlsy.*) so docs match a shipping version rather than chasing main; built via build-docs.sh with Pages source set to GitHub Actions.

nodes.label: Expected Rebase Conflict Set
nodes.rationale: Since AutoRaise removal the fork patches no upstream Swift file, so no Swift conflict is expected — if one appears, investigate drift rather than hand-resolving. Generated files are never hand-merged (take either side, re-run generate.sh); docs conflicts keep the fork banner/URLs and accept upstream body edits.

nodes.label: Rebase Protocol (fetch upstream, rebase, test, force-push)
nodes.norm_label: rebase protocol (fetch upstream, rebase, test, force-push)

nodes.label: Fork Release Workflow (tag push triggers CI)
nodes.rationale: Pushing a matching tag triggers release-adrianlsy.yml (build binary, GH Release, regenerate cask, PR against the tap) and pages.yml (build .site, deploy Pages). Failed releases are re-tagged as -Beta.adrianlsy.<n+1>; existing tags are never mutated.
nodes.norm_label: fork release workflow (tag push triggers ci)

nodes.label: Tag Naming Convention
nodes.rationale: -Beta. stays in the fork tag so the version string is honest (beta of a beta) and SemVer sorts the fork tag below a hypothetical stable release; the dot-separated pre-release chain is idiomatic SemVer and accepted by Homebrew. If upstream drops -Beta, the regexes in publish-release-adrianlsy.sh and release-adrianlsy.yml must be updated.

nodes.label: AdrianLSY/homebrew-tap Repo
nodes.rationale: Separate public repo holding Casks/aerospace-adrianlsy.rb, updated by the release workflow via a fine-grained PAT (HOMEBREW_TAP_PAT) with contents:write and pull_requests:write.

nodes.label: AdrianLSY/AeroSpace Fork
nodes.rationale: The fork carries no functional changes to AeroSpace; it exists to provide an independently built and released distribution: own Homebrew tap/cask, own docs site at adrianlsy.github.io/AeroSpace, and own issue templates/triage.

nodes.label: aerospace-adrianlsy Homebrew Cask and Tap
nodes.rationale: The cask conflicts_with 'aerospace' so both distributions cannot be installed simultaneously; the Homebrew install script deletes the com.apple.quarantine attribute because the app is not notarized.

nodes.label: Rebase-based Upstream Tracking
nodes.rationale: Fork's main stays rebased on nikitabobko/main; upstream commits arrive as-is, fork-specific commits sit on top, no merge commits.

nodes.label: Fork Version Scheme (v<upstream>-Beta.adrianlsy.<n>)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors upstream's -Beta pre-release marker because the combined binary is genuinely a beta of a beta; SemVer-compliant dot-separated pre-release chain; the patch counter <n> resets to 1 per upstream version.

nodes.label: AeroSpace (i3-like tiling window manager for macOS)
nodes.norm_label: aerospace (i3-like tiling window manager for macos)

nodes.label: Emulation of Virtual Workspaces
nodes.rationale: AeroSpace emulates its own virtual workspaces instead of relying on native macOS Spaces because of the Spaces' considerable limitations; this enables fast workspace switching without animations and without disabling SIP.

nodes.label: AX Dump Scenario: Firefox Google Meet Share Window
nodes.rationale: Reproduction recipe producing 7 different small popups plus the purple share pill indicator, captured as accessibility dumps for window-detection testing (upstream issue #1101).
nodes.norm_label: ax dump scenario: firefox google meet share window

nodes.label: Single Private API Principle (_AXUIElementGetWindow)
nodes.rationale: Sources/PrivateApi exposes exactly one private symbol, _AXUIElementGetWindow; the guiding principle is to keep it that way so AeroSpace stays maintainable and resistant to macOS updates without disabling SIP.

nodes.label: SPM vs Xcode Build Split
nodes.rationale: SPM cannot produce a macOS App Bundle, so the App Bundle is built via Xcode against a generated xcodeproj; push as much code as possible into the SPM library (Sources/AppBundle) so the Xcode target stays a thin entry point. Open Package.swift in Xcode, not the .xcodeproj.

nodes.label: Fork vs Upstream Contribution Scope
nodes.rationale: Contributions affecting core AeroSpace behavior (tiling, focus, multi-monitor, config parsing, upstream-matching CLI) should go upstream so the fix benefits everyone; the fork accepts only fork docs, release tooling, and issue templates.

nodes.label: AutoRaise (hover-to-raise) Removal
nodes.rationale: The bundled sbmpost/AutoRaise port ([auto-raise] config section) was removed in favour of upstream's native focus-follows-mouse (upstream v0.21.x). Breaking change: an unknown top-level key is a hard config error. Trade-off: focus now follows the pointer across monitors (better), but no longer re-evaluates when the window under a stationary pointer changes (worse). Last release with AutoRaise: v0.21.3-Beta.adrianlsy.1.

nodes.label: AeroSpace Project Values
nodes.rationale: Targeted at advanced users; keyboard centric; no GUI for configuration; practical features over ricing; dark magic (private APIs, code injection) avoided — only _AXUIElementGetWindow is used and SIP never needs disabling; goal is maintainability and resistance to macOS updates. Non-values: playing nicely with macOS Spaces, and ricing.

nodes.label: HotKey (global shortcuts wrapper)
nodes.rationale: Used as a more convenient wrapper around the macOS Carbon API to listen for global shortcuts.

nodes.label: Upstream Redirect Policy
nodes.rationale: Bugs clearly in upstream AeroSpace behavior (tiling, focus, multi-monitor, workspaces, config parsing, CLI) are welcome in the fork tracker but filing them at upstream helps the wider community; fork-specific templates only cover fork docs and release tooling because the fork has no functional delta from upstream.

nodes.label: Fork Release Tag Format (v<upstream>-Beta.adrianlsy.<n>)
nodes.rationale: Fork versions must match <upstream>-Beta.adrianlsy.<n>, mirroring upstream's -Beta pre-release marker; the release job validates the pushed tag against a regex and fails fast on mismatch, and the same tag pattern also triggers the docs Pages deployment.

nodes.label: OpenSpec Store Selection
nodes.rationale: --store <id> is sticky for a whole workflow so every spec/change read and write targets the same registered store; without a store, commands act on the nearest local openspec/ root.

nodes.label: Inline Sync Before Archive
nodes.rationale: Archive must run the delta-spec sync inline and re-verify every capability's main spec before moving changeRoot: a background sync would have changeRoot moved out from under it, leaving the change archived while main specs were never updated. On any mismatch the archive stops with changeRoot intact so the sync can be retried.

nodes.label: Explore Mode Stance
nodes.rationale: Explore mode is a stance, not a workflow: no fixed steps, no mandatory outputs. It is for thinking, not implementing - creating OpenSpec artifacts is capturing thinking, while writing application code is forbidden until the user exits explore mode and starts a change.

nodes.label: Artifact Dependency Graph
nodes.rationale: openspec status is file-existence only, so a done artifact does not prove its dependencies exist; the required set is built by walking requires edges transitively from applyRequires, and dependencies are enablers, not gates - a blocked artifact whose only missing dependency was deliberately skipped is still created.

nodes.label: Planning Boundary Principle
nodes.rationale: The request that triggers the propose workflow authorizes planning only, even if it asks to build or fix something; implementation must wait for a new explicit user request, preventing scope creep from plan into code within one response.

nodes.label: Capability Retirement Rules
nodes.rationale: A spec whose last requirement is removed is deleted rather than left with an empty Requirements section, but only when six conditions hold, including the change's .openspec.yaml declaring retire_capabilities: true and the spec.md resolving inside the real specs root (symlink guard against deleting external files).

nodes.label: Intelligent Merging Principle
nodes.rationale: Agent-driven merging is chosen over programmatic overwrite so a scenario can be added without copying the entire requirement; anything the delta does not mention is preserved in the main spec's existing order, and the operation must be idempotent.
